question: Can independent subcolony counting error alone create an apparent within-island beta-variability signal as large as the observed hierarchical separation?

eligible_units.reason: Same stable-roster units as the frozen primary hierarchical decomposition.

latent_complete_synchrony_null.fixed_composition: For each island, q_j is the colony-code share of cumulative breeding pairs across all 1991-2017 censuses.
latent_complete_synchrony_null.latent_mean: lambda_jt = observed island total N_t * q_j
latent_complete_synchrony_null.interpretation: Every latent subcolony trajectory within an island is exactly proportional to the island total, so latent within-island beta variability equals one before observation error is added.
latent_complete_synchrony_null.island_trajectories: Observed island totals are retained as latent annual means so the empirical among-island trajectory structure is not destroyed.

error_model_reuse: Same Poisson and independent Gamma-Poisson multiplicative-CV families used in the frozen N_eff mechanical-coupling diagnostic; the Gamma-Poisson CV values are sensitivity levels, not Palmer-specific observer-error estimates.

primary_statistics.raw_beta_within: Wang-Loreau beta from all 25 colony-code units to the three island totals; one-sided Monte Carlo tail against the observed frozen value.
primary_statistics.raw_beta_among: Wang-Loreau beta from islands to the three-island aggregate.
primary_statistics.raw_log_beta_contrast: log(beta_within / beta_among); one-sided Monte Carlo tail against the observed frozen value.
primary_statistics.raw_all_three_order_probability: Null probability that each of COR, HUM and LIT individually has within-island beta greater than the among-island beta.

fixed_centered_sensitivities.linear_detrended_log1p: Median within-island covariance beta divided by among-island covariance beta.
fixed_centered_sensitivities.annual_log1p_growth: Median within-island covariance beta divided by among-island covariance beta.
fixed_centered_sensitivities.boundary: These are non-additive sensitivities only; they are not alpha/gamma decompositions.

decision_rules.measurement_error_robust_raw_hierarchy: Both observed raw beta_within and observed raw log-beta contrast must be in the upper 5% tail under all three frozen error models.
decision_rules.centered_signal_robustness: Detrended and annual-growth median within/among ratios are reported as fixed diagnostics and are not promoted as rescue endpoints if compatible with the error-only null.
decision_rules.no_model_tuning: Do not add intermediate CV values, alternative fixed-share definitions, correlated-error structures, or extra transformations unless an external empirical error calibration is obtained.

interpretation_boundary: The Gamma-Poisson CV10% and CV20% models are uncalibrated sensitivities, not estimates of Palmer observer error.
Failure under CV20% does not prove that counting error caused the hierarchy; it means the current data cannot exclude that level of independent multiplicative error.
Passing Poisson or CV10% does not prove biological buffering.
Centered log1p and growth diagnostics are non-additive sensitivities and do not restore the exact Wang-Loreau alpha/beta/gamma identity.
The diagnostic tests measurement-error robustness of the hierarchy, not the N_eff coefficient.
No new error models are opened without external empirical calibration.
motivation: Independent census error among subcolonies can create apparent asynchrony that averages out when counts are summed. The error-model family is inherited unchanged from the frozen N_eff mechanical-coupling diagnostic.
positive_state_condition: For a frozen positive island-year, redraw the full simulated subcolony count vector only if all simulated counts are zero, matching the known-positive-state conditioning in the N_eff error diagnostic.
